name: Local
v7_who: City councils, county boards, charter commissions, voters in home-rule places
v7_instrument: Ordinance, charter amendment or local practice
who_decides: Council or board, mayor, or local voters
what_it_takes: A council majority and the mayor’s signature or an override, within the powers the state grants
how_it_can_be_undone: A later ordinance, or the state, which can preempt it
sources: Massachusetts Constitution, Amendment Article LXXXIX (Home Rule), sections 6 and 7

name: State statute
v7_instrument: A bill passed by the legislature and signed, or a rule issued by a state agency or utility commission under a statute
what_it_takes: A majority of each chamber (one chamber in Nebraska) and the governor’s signature; overrides from three-fifths to two-thirds, by state
how_it_can_be_undone: A later state law, a court, or voters where the state allows
sources: State constitutions read in round 0: Massachusetts, Nebraska, Virginia, Arizona

name: State ballot
v7_who: Voters, petition campaigns, courts that review ballot language
v7_instrument: Citizen initiative, referendum or legislative referral
what_it_takes: Enough valid signatures, then a majority of voters (in California, 546,651 signatures for a statute and 874,641 for an amendment)
how_it_can_be_undone: Another measure; in some states the legislature; a court
sources: California Secretary of State, Statewide Initiative Guide and "How to Qualify an Initiative"

name: Federal statute
v7_instrument: Act of Congress, including appropriations and reconciliation
what_it_takes: A majority of each chamber, 60 senators to end debate on most bills, and the President’s signature, or two-thirds of each chamber to override a veto
sources: U.S. Constitution, Article I, Section 7; U.S. Senate, "About Filibusters and Cloture"

name: Chamber rule or confirmation
v7_instrument: House or Senate rule; Senate confirmation of nominees
what_it_takes: A majority of the chamber; in the Senate, two-thirds of senators present and voting to end debate on a rules change, while precedents set by majority vote changed cloture on nominations in 2013 and 2017
sources: U.S. Constitution, Article I, Section 5; Standing Rules of the Senate, Rules V, XXII and XXXI; Senate votes of November 21, 2013 and April 6, 2017

name: Federal executive action
v7_instrument: Executive order, agency rule, guidance, staffing and budget execution
what_it_takes: The President’s order, or an agency rule after notice and comment
how_it_can_be_undone: A later order or rule; Congress under the Congressional Review Act; a court

name: Enforcement and litigation
v7_who: The Justice Department, the Federal Trade Commission, the National Labor Relations Board, state attorneys general and private plaintiffs
v7_instrument: Cases and settlements under existing law
who_decides: An agency, a state attorney general or a private party, then a court
what_it_takes: A complaint and a court’s judgment, or a settlement; a federal antitrust consent judgment needs the court to find it in the public interest
how_it_can_be_undone: An appeal; a decree’s own end date
sources: 15 U.S.C. 16 (Tunney Act); 16 CFR 2.34; 29 U.S.C. 160; U.S. Courts, "Civil Cases"

name: Court doctrine
v7_instrument: Rulings that change what other routes may do
what_it_takes: A majority of the court that decides; the Supreme Court takes a case only for "compelling reasons"
how_it_can_be_undone: A later ruling (Loper Bright overruled Chevron in 2024), a statute where the ruling read one, or an amendment
sources: Supreme Court Rule 10; 28 U.S.C. 1254 and 2101(c); Loper Bright Enterprises v. Raimondo (2024)

name: Article V
v7_who: Two-thirds of each house of Congress and three-quarters of the states, or a convention
what_it_takes: Two-thirds of each house (or a convention called by two-thirds of the states), then three-fourths of the states, 38 of 50
sources: U.S. Constitution, Article V; National Archives, "The Constitutional Amendment Process"

name: Interstate compact
v7_instrument: Matching statutes in several states that take effect at a threshold
who_decides: State legislatures, and Congress where its consent is required
what_it_takes: Each member state enacts the same statute; it takes effect at the threshold the compact sets
sources: U.S. Constitution, Article I, Section 10; RCW 29A.56.300; Minnesota Statutes 208.051

name: Civil society
v7_instrument: Organizing, philanthropy, newsrooms, unions, membership groups, private contracts
what_it_takes: No government approval; the First Amendment protects assembly and petition, and tax law limits what charities may do in politics
sources: U.S. Constitution, First Amendment; IRS pages on 501(c)(3) and 501(c)(4) organizations; 29 U.S.C. 157
